dedupe_keys.name: jw fd long horizon multimodal solar flare forecasting dataset 2011 to 2025

description: JW-FD is a 15-year multimodal dataset for training and testing solar flare forecasts, spanning 1 January 2011 to 31 December 2025. It is built from SDO/HMI line-of-sight magnetograms, NOAA Solar Region Summary reports and NOAA X-ray flare event lists, and holds 3,064 active regions and 1,991,247 co-registered magnetogram crops in FITS, PNG, CSV and MP4 form. Each sample carries 29 magnetic features linked to configurable flare labels under a strict pre-eruption window, with seven forecast horizons and four GOES intensity thresholds, an 8:1:1 split by active region to avoid temporal leakage, and PNG branches at six magnetic saturation thresholds. It was released by Shao Mingfu of the National Astronomical Observatories with an open-source construction pipeline on GitHub. The 10 percent subset published on 30 July 2026 is accessible on Zenodo as free multi-part archives of about 178 GB under CC BY 4.0. Caveats: flares are one driver of space weather and the dataset does not include radiation storm or geomagnetic impact labels, and the Zenodo release is a subset. It supports development of forecasting models behind space weather warnings that protect satellites, aviation, radio communications and power grids; related records are the SWPC geoelectric field maps and INTERMAGNET.
